title: NY State Senate · District 23
area: Most of the North and East Shores of Staten Island, plus parts of southern Brooklyn.

context.text: Incumbent Jessica Scarcella-Spanton defeated Omar Mohamad in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 72.8% to 26.8% (6,603 to 2,429 votes).
Ruslan Shamal advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party lines without a primary contest.

summary.text: Jessica Scarcella-Spanton is the Democratic incumbent state senator for District 23, covering Staten Island's North and East Shores and parts of southern Brooklyn. A Staten Island native who previously worked as a legislative and operations director in the state legislature, she chairs the Senate's Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs Committee and is seeking a second full term.

background.text: Born and raised on Staten Island to two educators; moved to Colorado Springs in 2012 while her husband deployed to Afghanistan with the U.S. Army, then returned to Staten Island.
Began as an intern for the NYS Assembly in 2009 and rose to Legislative Director.
Served as Director of Operations for then-state Senator Diane Savino from 2017 to 2021, including work on the district's COVID-19 vaccine distribution and hospital-support advocacy.
Worked as Assistant Director of Government and Community Relations at the MTA before her election.

Chairs the Senate Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs Committee; also sits on the Civil Service and Pensions, Cultural Affairs/Tourism/Parks/Recreation, Disabilities, and Labor committees.

priorities.text: Has pushed for Staten Island to be included in citywide pre-K ("2-K") expansion, arguing the borough's children were being excluded from a program other boroughs received.
priorities.quote: While the rest of the city revels in the prospects of this program, Staten Island's children are left without any opportunity or equitable access to be part of it. That is a disservice to every child and every hardworking parent in our borough.

priorities.text: Has made veterans' issues a focus of her legislative work, including sponsoring a registry for service members and veterans who may have been exposed to hazardous substances at military installations.

positions.summary: Voted yes on the Grid Reliability and Energy Affordability Transition (GREAT) Act, which creates a virtual power plant program aimed at reducing reliance on fossil-fuel "peaker" plants during peak demand.

record.text: Sponsored S10515, the "Wireless Security Enforcement (WiSE) Act," which would make manufacturing, importing, or selling wireless signal jammers a class D felony; in the Senate Internet and Technology Committee as of May 15, 2026, not yet passed by either chamber.

Sponsored S10151-A, which would direct the state veterans' services commissioner to establish a registry of service members, veterans, and family members who may have experienced hazardous substance exposure at military installations; amended and recommitted to the Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs Committee on June 1, 2026.
Chairs the Senate Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs Committee.

summary.text: Ruslan Shamal is a Staten Island broadcaster and small-business owner running as the Republican/Conservative nominee. Born in Belarus, he has lived on Staten Island since 2014 and previously ran unsuccessfully for New York City Council District 49 in 2023.

background.text: Emigrated from Belarus; lived in Brooklyn and Massachusetts before settling on Staten Island in 2014.
Has worked in broadcast media for more than 20 years and runs an e-commerce business.
Opened FurStar Resort, a dog daycare business in Staten Island's Tompkinsville neighborhood.
Lost the 2023 general election for New York City Council District 49 to incumbent Kamillah Hanks.

priorities.text: Frames his campaign around opposition to democratic socialism in New York City and his personal experience under authoritarian government in Belarus.
Says he would support the NYPD and public-safety initiatives, and would vote to repeal or reform the state's bail laws.
Says he would oppose new taxes and "hidden fees."

positions.summary: Campaign platform includes supporting the NYPD and public-safety initiatives.
